warnModal.title: Skill health check
warnModal.body: “{name}” contains terms that look like an “operations flow”. A review skill should only describe “what to audit, how to judge”, not git operations / code changes / worktree skipping (handled by the engine). Matched:
warnModal.note:
Most are “descriptive mentions” (false positives — e.g. writing “no git push” in the methodology also gets flagged), with no impact.
Even when enabled, the engine hard-blocks git writes / file changes at the tool level; a skill cannot run them — so this is just a warning, not an error.

agentConfig.title: Agent configuration
agentConfig.subtitle: What Claude Code and Codex each read in this directory, what they report once started, and the two switches PR Cockpit owns. Switch provider to see its report.
agentConfig.loadedNaHint: The CLI only reports memory files; directories, settings and MCP config are not reported.
agentConfig.chromeHint: Start Claude Code with --chrome so the Claude in Chrome MCP server comes up. Applies to every Claude session (from the next turn) and needs the Chrome extension; reviews only get it when MCP is allowed below.
agentConfig.reviewMcpHint: Off by default: the review family (review / re-review / recheck / automation) connects no MCP server and only reads the repository. On, reviews connect every MCP server configured in your CLI, like sessions do — including tools that write to external systems, and automatic reviews run unattended. Shared by both providers. Servers declared inside the PR branch itself (.mcp.json / .codex/config.toml) are never enabled for a review.

groups.switchesHint: Only these two live in the PR Cockpit database and are edited here; everything below is the CLI’s own report, read-only.
groups.files: Files read into the startup context
groups.filesHintClaude: Files on disk the CLI may read + the files it reports as actually in context (auto-memory and the rules it really loaded included). “not loaded” only applies to a CLAUDE.md that exists but was not read; rule files get a row only when loaded — one with a paths condition that was not used does not appear. Settings contents are never read.
groups.filesHintCodex: Files on disk Codex may read + the instruction files the app-server reports as injected and the config layers in effect. Whether the memories directory is injected is not reported by the protocol.
groups.contextHintClaude: What the context is made of before the first message: by category, and how much each memory file and skill takes. “deferred” tool definitions load on demand and are not counted in the total.
groups.contextHintCodex: The Codex app-server has no startup-context token figure (usage only exists per turn); listed instead are the instruction files it injects and their size, without estimating.
groups.mcpHintClaude: Status, origin and version of each MCP server when the probe started; open a row for its tools — the “read-only / writes” notes are the server’s own annotations.
groups.mcpHintCodex: Login status, version and tools of each MCP server; open a row for the tool list. Review threads connect them only when MCP is allowed.
groups.commandsHint: Every slash command the CLI reports, grouped by origin, collapsed by default; open a row for the full description, arguments and aliases.
groups.skillsHint: Skills Codex discovered, grouped by plugin, collapsed by default; grey = disabled. Open a row for the full description, / name and path. Codex has no slash-command concept.

agentConfig.pluginsHint: Plugins the CLI actually loaded (name · version · source).
agentConfig.settingsLayersHint: Which settings layers the CLI applied (layer names only, contents are never read).
agentConfig.configLayersHint: The order in which the app-server merges config (later overrides earlier); layers whose file does not exist show empty.
agentConfig.codexNoTokens: Codex does not report startup-context tokens. Instruction files a thread in this directory actually injects:

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Cost, tokens and quality signals from every agent run. Estimated Codex prices come from data/codex-rates.json.
dashboard.noData: No runs recorded yet — run a review to see numbers here.
dashboard.pricingNote: Codex cost is estimated from {n} priced models (rates as of {asOf}).
dashboard.pricingMissing: Codex runs are not priced: add data/codex-rates.json to estimate their cost.
dashboard.noTriaged: No triaged review yet — tick or post findings once and this fills in.
dashboard.tilesHint: Every run in the selected project and period.

hint.spend: One row per run, aggregated here by kind, model and day. Cost is what the SDK reported (Claude) or tokens × rate (Codex, marked ~); runs without a rate count as "unpriced" and are left out of the total.
hint.bySubkind: Run kind × provider. review / guided / recheck / skillgen are the review family; session is the persistent chat; helper is a one-shot helper call (commit message, title, translation).
hint.byModel: Review family only (review / guided / recheck). Average cost counts priced runs only; p50 / p95 = half / 95% of the runs finished within this duration.
hint.byDay: Grouped by the run's creation day; at most the 30 most recent days that had runs (within the period above).
hint.quality: Precision only counts reviews a human handled (ticked or posted) — a draft nobody looked at says nothing about the skill and is left out; rechecks and automation are counted from their own records.
hint.precision: Precision = human-accepted (ticked or posted) ÷ all findings; machine ticks (auto / engine) do not count as accepted. Cost per accepted = every run of those reviews ÷ accepted findings — what one useful finding costs.
hint.recheck: Retraction rate: findings withdrawn after your feedback and a re-review (lower is better). Fixed rate: findings judged fixed after the author pushed. Below, the count of each finding's latest recheck status.
hint.automation: Event counts from the automation engine: review_created / recheck / posted / fix_started / pushed, plus cooldown, capped, converged and the error kinds.
hint.recent: One row per run, newest first. After the cost, ~ means estimated and +? means some turns were unpriced (the total is a lower bound); hover a row for its title or error text.
